title: Acne Vulgaris
guideline: AAD Guidelines of Care for the Management of Acne Vulgaris (2024)

clinical_targets.goal: Score 0 (Clear) or 1 (Almost Clear) with ≥ 2-grade improvement from baseline
≥ 75% reduction in inflammatory papules, pustules, and open/closed comedones
Early aggressive control of deep inflammatory lesions to prevent post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) and permanent atrophic scarring

steps.title: Mild Acne: Topical Retinoids & Antimicrobial Combinations
steps.rationale: Target microcomedone formation and follicular hyperkeratinization. Topical retinoids are the foundation of acne treatment; combine with Benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) to prevent bacterial resistance.

drug_classes.role: First-line comedolytic and anti-inflammatory core therapy for all acne types.
drug_classes.dosing: Apply a pea-sized amount to the entire clean, dry face once daily at bedtime.
drug_classes.pearls: Adapalene has higher photostability and superior cutaneous tolerability (less erythema/peeling) compared to traditional Tretinoin. Advise daily broad-spectrum SPF.

drug_classes.role: Bactericidal against Cutibacterium acnes without inducing bacterial resistance.
drug_classes.dosing: BPO 2.5%–5% gel once daily; Azelaic Acid 15%–20% cream/gel twice daily.
drug_classes.pearls: BPO 2.5% is as clinically effective as 10% but with significantly less skin irritation. Azelaic acid is particularly beneficial for post-inflammatory erythema/hyperpigmentation.

steps.title: Moderate Acne: Fixed-Dose Topicals + Oral Antibiotics
steps.rationale: When topical therapy alone is insufficient for moderate inflammatory papulopustular lesions, add an oral tetracycline for a strictly limited duration (max 3–4 months) alongside BPO to prevent resistance.

drug_classes.role: Synergistic comedolytic + antimicrobial action with enhanced patient adherence.
drug_classes.dosing: Adapalene + BPO gel once daily bedtime; or Clindamycin 1% + BPO 5% gel once daily morning.
drug_classes.pearls: Never prescribe topical or oral antibiotics as monotherapy without Benzoyl Peroxide due to rapid resistance emergence.

drug_classes.role: Systemic reduction of follicular C. acnes and neutrophil chemotaxis.
drug_classes.dosing: Doxycycline 50–100 mg twice daily with food and large glass of water.
drug_classes.pearls: Take upright to avoid pill-induced esophagitis. Contraindicated in children < 8 years and pregnancy due to tooth discoloration. Limit course to 12 weeks.

sample_brands: Doxyral 80%, Powder for use in drinking water/milk

steps.title: Severe Nodulocystic / Conglobate or Treatment-Refractory Acne
steps.rationale: Oral Isotretinoin is the only disease-modifying therapy that addresses all 4 pathogenic factors: sebum production, comedogenesis, C. acnes colonization, and inflammation.

drug_classes.role: Definitive curative-intent therapy for nodulocystic, scarring, or psychologically distressing refractory acne.
drug_classes.dosing: Initial 0.5 mg/kg/day for 1 month, then titrate to 1.0 mg/kg/day targeting cumulative target dose of 120–150 mg/kg.
drug_classes.pearls: Take with high-fat meal for optimal absorption. Cheilitis and xerosis are universal (counsel on heavy emollient lip balm). Warn of transient initial flare.

special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: Oral Isotretinoin and topical retinoids are strictly contraindicated (Category X / Extreme Teratogenicity). Requires 2 negative pregnancy tests prior to starting and monthly testing + strict dual contraception. Safe topical alternatives: Azelaic acid and topical Erythromycin.
special_populations.hepatic_impairment: Isotretinoin is contraindicated in preexisting significant liver dysfunction.

monitoring: Baseline and periodic (at 1-2 months) fasting lipid profile (triglycerides, total cholesterol) and liver function tests (ALT/AST) for oral Isotretinoin. Screen for mood changes and depression.
